chapters.title: Azure foundations
chapters.intro: Regions, App Service, Azure SQL Database and Blob Storage.

concepts.def: Hosts static sites (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images) built from a code repository. Files are served from points of presence around the world, and HTTPS certificates for custom domains are included.
concepts.ref: What is Azure Static Web Apps?

concepts.def: Managed hosting for web apps and APIs. You pick a plan tier and deploy code or a container; Azure runs, patches and load-balances the servers.

Azure runs the servers, operating system and patching; you bring code or files. You give up some control in exchange for much less operational work.

Prefer PaaS unless you need something only a virtual machine allows.
Traffic between users and your services travels over TLS (HTTPS), so nobody on the network path can read or change it. Most Azure PaaS services offer an HTTPS-only setting.
The Well-Architected pillar about spending only what the workload needs: right-size tiers, scale with demand and remove what you don't use.

challenges.title: Hello, Azure
challenges.brief:
A designer wants a personal portfolio site: a dozen pages of project write-ups and images, and a link to email them. Most visitors arrive from a link in a CV, some from other countries.

They never want to patch a server, and while traffic is low the site should cost next to nothing.
functional: Visitors open the portfolio in a web browser
Pages and images load from Azure
nonFunctional: Every page is served over HTTPS
No servers or operating systems to patch
Costs as little as possible while traffic is low
Loads quickly for visitors in other countries

estimate.q: About how much data does the site send to visitors per month?
estimate.workings: 2,000 visits × 4 pages × 1.5 MB = 12,000 MB ≈ 12 GB per month.

tradeoff.q: Why is Static Web Apps a better fit than a virtual machine for this site?
choices: Azure runs and patches the servers and serves the files from locations around the world, so there is nothing to look after.
Static Web Apps can run any server-side software a virtual machine can.
tradeoff.why: A VM means an operating system to patch, a web server to configure and a bill even when nobody visits. For a handful of static pages, a managed host removes all of that.

challenges.learn:
For static content, the simplest and cheapest host is one where Azure runs the servers: **Static Web Apps** serves the files from points of presence worldwide, with HTTPS included.

**App Service** fits when the site needs server-side code, but you then choose a plan tier and make sure HTTPS-only is on. The trade-off is control: a managed platform decides the operating system, runtime and scaling options for you.

rules.text: The site runs on a managed web platform, with no servers to patch
rules.hint: Look for a service where Azure runs the servers and you only bring the files or the code.

rules.text: Visitors' browsers load the pages from that platform
rules.hint: Connect the browser to the service that hosts the site, in the direction of the request.

rules.text: Every page is served over HTTPS
rules.hint: Static Web Apps always uses HTTPS. App Service has an HTTPS-only setting: make sure it is on.

rules.text: Pages are served from locations close to visitors around the world
rules.hint: Some hosts copy static files to many locations worldwide on their own.

rules.text: The whole design costs at most 1 unit while traffic is low
rules.hint: Free and entry tiers exist for exactly this kind of site.

rules.text: No virtual machine to patch and restart
rules.hint: A virtual machine brings an operating system you must update, secure and monitor yourself.
